graph_nodes.func: new (D-1 as ruled; I-3). Prepares a name list once: refuses an element that is not a `str`; keeps each distinct name once, at its first occurrence; folds each (`_fold`) and sets its character mask (`_char_mask`); cuts each into tokens (`_tokens`), gives every distinct folded token an id in code-point order, and stores each name's token ids; builds the postings (token id → the names holding it) and the pre-order array trie of the tokens (`_build_trie`). The fields are `[Data: LabelIndex]`: strings, one tuple and flat `array` buffers — no dict trie, no per-name tuple of token strings, no dict of Python lists (the 77.9 MiB of v3; E2-1).

graph_nodes.name: _fold
examples: (R-A2L-MATCH.4/1) `DRÜCK_MAX` → `drÜck_max` (`Ü` kept; `drück` is 1 edit from the token `drÜck`, X §C), so `DRÜCK_MAX` is `fuzzy` for `drück`, not `prefix` (B4 §1)
graph_nodes.func: new (D-2 A). `A`–`Z` (U+0041 … U+005A) → `a`–`z`; every other character kept, so the result is as long as `text` and spans index the name directly. `str.translate` with a 26-entry table; never `str.lower` or `str.casefold` (Unicode tables, version-dependent).

graph_nodes.name: _char_mask
graph_nodes.func: new. The OR of one bit per character of an already folded `text`: `a`–`z` → bits 0–25, `0`–`9` → bits 26–35, any other character `c` → bit `36 + ord(c) % 27` (at most 62, so a mask fits `array('Q')`). A name holds the key characters in order only if its mask holds every bit of the keys' mask; a shared bit lets more names through to `_subsequence`, never fewer.

graph_nodes.name: _tokens
examples: (derived, X §A, §H) U+00A0 then `VALUE_0001` → `((0, 6), (7, 11))` (U+00A0 is a letter); U+001C then `VALUE_0001` → `((1, 6), (7, 11))` (U+001C is a separator); three U+0663 → `((0, 3),)` (one letter token)
graph_nodes.func: new. The [start, end) spans of the CTX-A2L-MATCH *tokens* of `text`, read on the unfolded text (the case cuts need the case): maximal runs of `0`–`9`; maximal runs of letters (A–Z, a–z, or any character above U+007F), cut before an uppercase letter that follows a lowercase one and before the last uppercase letter of a run of two or more that a lowercase letter follows. Every other character is a separator and in no token. Classes by code point, never `str.isalpha`, `isdigit` or `isalnum` (E2-5).

graph_nodes.name: _allowed_edits
examples: (derived, X §H) three U+0663 → `1` (three letters by CTX-A2L-MATCH; `str.isdigit()` says `True`, which would give 0: E2-5)
(R-A2L-MATCH.11/1 neg) 1 edit for a digit token → `VALUE_0300` lists `VALUE_0200` → RED
graph_nodes.func: new (D-4 A). 0 for a token of digits (its first character is `0`–`9`: tokens are pure runs) or of 1 or 2 letters; 1 for 3 to 5 letters; 2 for 6 or more.

graph_nodes.name: _prefix_distance
examples: (R-A2L-MATCH.12/3, X §C, §H) `cvure`, `curve`, cap 1 → `2` (= cap + 1; the distance is 2)
graph_nodes.func: new (D-5 A). The smallest optimal-string-alignment distance between `query_token` and a prefix of `name_token` (the empty prefix included) when it is at most `cap`, else `cap + 1`; it may stop as soon as a whole column of the alignment is above `cap`. Characters compare as given: both folded, or both raw for the case-exact check. Used by `_classify`; `_fuzzy_token_distances` gives the same values for many tokens at once.

graph_nodes.name: _join_spans
examples: (R-A2L-MATCH.31/2, X §D) the eight one-character spans of `value_000` on `VALUE_0010` → `((0, 5), (6, 8), (9, 10))`
(R-A2L-MATCH.34/1 neg) touching spans kept apart → `((0, 3), (3, 8))` → RED
graph_nodes.func: new. The fewest spans in offset order that cover the same offsets: sort, then join each span that starts at or before the end of the one before it.

graph_nodes.name: _at_boundary
examples: (X §E) every offset of every name of C08, C08i, SRC, BAL, SWB, SWA and six more (`572,421` offsets) → equal to the oracle's boundary set (from `_tokens` and the separators): `0` disagreements
graph_nodes.func: new (in place of v3's per-name boundary bitmask; E2-1). Whether `offset` of `name` is a CTX-A2L-MATCH *boundary offset*: offset 0; a separator; or the first offset of a token, read on the unfolded name from its neighbours — the character before is a separator; one of the two is a digit and the other a letter; a lowercase letter then an uppercase one; or an uppercase letter before an uppercase letter that a lowercase letter follows.

graph_nodes.name: _subsequence
examples: (R-A2L-MATCH.9/1, .31/1, derived from the spans of B4 §1) `mp`, `map_0001` → `(0, 2)`, spans `(0,1),(2,3)`
(R-A2L-MATCH.31/3 neg) each key at its rightmost possible offset → other spans on the BalanceTube name → RED
graph_nodes.func: new. The leftmost offsets of the key characters in `text`, each after the one before (`str.find` from the previous offset + 1), or `None` when one is missing.

graph_nodes.name: _parse_query
examples: (R-A2L-MATCH.24) `Value_0001`, `False` → text `Value_0001`, tokens (`Value`, `0001`): the case-exact check compares these with the raw name
(R-A2L-MATCH.1, derived, X §A, §H) U+001C then `VALUE_0001`, `True` → text U+001C + `value_0001` (U+001C kept), tokens (`value`, `0001`); U+00A0 then `VALUE_0001` → tokens (U+00A0 + `value`, `0001`)
graph_nodes.func: new. Strips exactly the six CTX-A2L-MATCH whitespace characters (space, tab, line feed, carriage return, vertical tab, form feed) from both ends — never a bare `str.strip()`, which also strips U+001C … U+001F, U+0085, U+00A0 and others (E2-5); `None` when what is left holds no letter or digit; else `[Data: _Query]`: `text` = the stripped query, folded when `fold`; `tokens` = the `_tokens` spans of the stripped (unfolded) query, taken from `text`; `keys` = the letters and digits of `text`, in order; `folded` = `fold`.

graph_nodes.name: _classify
examples: (R-A2L-MATCH.16/1, O) `value_000` (folded), `VALUE_0001` → `(PREFIX, 0, ((0, 9),))` (also a substring and a fuzzy match); raw → `None`
(R-A2L-MATCH.28/1, O) `count`, `DiscountCount` → `(SUBSTRING, 0, ((8, 13),))`; raw → `(SUBSTRING, 1, ((3, 8),))`, the same rule, so case-exact
(R-A2L-MATCH.24/3, O) raw `drück`: `druck_max` → `(FUZZY, 1, ((0, 5),))` (case-exact); `DRÜCK_MAX` → `None` (not case-exact); `Drück_Max` → `FUZZY` while its folded rule is `PREFIX` (not case-exact)
(R-A2L-MATCH.16/1 neg) the last rule met instead of the first → `VALUE_0001` is `FUZZY` for `value_000` → RED
graph_nodes.func: new (the rows' definitional check for one name; the E1 oracle `evaluate_b`). The first rule in rank order that `name` (folded when `query.folded`) meets for `query`, with its rule key and its match spans, or `None`. EXACT: `((0, len(name)),)`. PREFIX: `((0, len(query.text)),)`. SUBSTRING: key 0 and the leftmost occurrence at a boundary offset (`_at_boundary`), else key 1 and the leftmost occurrence. TOKEN: for each query token, from the start of the leftmost name token that starts with it, as long as it. FUZZY (the name has a token): for each query token the leftmost name token at the smallest `_prefix_distance(qt, nt, _allowed_edits(qt))`, which must be at most `_allowed_edits(qt)`; key = the sum; span = that name token. SUBSEQUENCE: one span per offset of `_subsequence`. Spans pass through `_join_spans`. `rank` calls it for each listed name, and with the raw query for case-exactness (the same rule).

graph_nodes.name: _order_key

out.raw: tuple[int, int, int, int, str] order

examples: (R-A2L-MATCH.20/1, O, B4 §1) query `value_000`: `VALUE_0001` → `(1, 0, 10, 1, 'VALUE_0001')`; every `prefix` key `(1, …)` sorts before every `subsequence` key `(5, …)`
(R-A2L-MATCH.25/2 neg) a stable sort with no name part → C08r gives `VALUE_0001` first for `0001` → RED
graph_nodes.func: new (D-3 B, D-6 A). `(position of rule in MatchRule, key, len(name), 0 if case_exact else 1, name)`; tuple and `str` comparison give the rank order, code-point order last, so the order is total over distinct names and the input order decides nothing.

graph_nodes.name: _token_range
examples: (R-A2L-MATCH.11/2) [`BA_X`] (tokens `ba`, `x`), `ab` → an empty range: no token and no fuzzy match, so `rank` gives `[]`
graph_nodes.func: new. The ids `lo` … `hi - 1` of the sorted distinct tokens that start with `prefix` (contiguous in code-point order): `bisect_left(tokens, prefix)`, then `bisect_left` of `prefix[:-1] + chr(ord(prefix[-1]) + 1)` from `lo`; a prefix that ends in U+10FFFF scans forward instead.

graph_nodes.name: _build_trie

out.raw: tuple(str chars, array depth, array first, array end)

examples: (R-A2L-MATCH.37, B4 §4, W) REF's 77,256 tokens → `177148` nodes; chars 177,197 bytes and each array 749,076 bytes, 2.3 MiB in all
graph_nodes.func: new (E2-1). The pre-order array trie of the sorted distinct tokens: one node per distinct non-empty prefix, in pre-order (= the tokens' code-point order); `chars[j]` is its last character, `depth[j]` its length, `first[j]` the id of the first token under it, `end[j]` the index after its subtree; `first` ends with one sentinel, `len(tokens)`; the arrays are `array('I')`. The tokens under node `j` are the ids `first[j]` … `first[end[j]] - 1`. One pass over the tokens with the common prefix of each and the one before, and a stack of open nodes.

graph_nodes.name: _fuzzy_token_distances
examples: (R-A2L-MATCH.10/1, X §F) C08, `cuvre`, `1` → {`curve`: 1} (ids written as their tokens)
(X §F) REF, 33 query tokens with 1 or 2 allowed edits (from `nzukij` to `pposbxiifkdgfiajnbbpvb`) → equal to brute force (the prefix distance to each of the 77,256 tokens): `0` mismatches

(R-A2L-MATCH.36, W) REF, median of 5 per query token: `nzukij` `45.0` ms (v3 dict trie 46.3, bare sorted list 81.9); `pposbxiifkdgfiajnbbpvb` `40.3` ms (v3 102.0, sorted list 136.7); all 24 tokens `358.0` ms (v3 461.7, sorted list 773.4)
graph_nodes.func: new (E2-1). `{token id: prefix distance}` for every distinct token of `index` at a prefix distance of at most `allowed` from `query_token`. For `allowed` 0: every id of `_token_range(index._tokens, query_token)`, with 0. Otherwise one walk of the trie arrays in pre-order: each node's alignment column from its parent's (and its grandparent's, for a transposition), capped at `allowed + 1` and computed only on the band |row − depth| ≤ `allowed`; the best prefix distance so far carried down the path; when the column minimum is above `allowed` or not below the best, every token under the node gets the best (when it is at most `allowed`) and the walk jumps to `end[j]`. The same values as `_prefix_distance` token by token.
